target.name: Ulysses Robotics
target.founder: Akhil Voorakkara, Jamie Wedderburn, Colm O'Brien, Will O'Brien

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $38M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Ulysses Robotics, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Akhil Voorakkara, Jamie Wedderburn, Colm O'Brien, and Will O'Brien, has raised $38M to date. Valuation analysis draws on two applicable methods triangulated against a peer set of 9 companies (1 public, 8 private), including same-sector and adjacent-stage comparables such as Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed).

The Stage-Progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $76M. The Peer-Median method anchors to the median valuation across the three identified robotics peers at $1.6B, reflecting the range of $1.1B to $1.8B observed in the comparable set. These two methods produce a wide spread reflecting early-stage uncertainty and heterogeneity within the peer group.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $65M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $863M. The substantial gap between stage-based and peer-based methods reflects tension between Ulysses' current capital raised ($38M) and the maturity valuations of later-stage robotics peers. Key uncertainties include revenue trajectory, unit economics, and whether peer comps—concentrated in Series B—appropriately reflect Series A risk and progress milestones.
